newsitem.title: USA: Indiana soy 27 percent harvested vs 68 pct average.
newsitem.headline: Indiana soy 27 percent harvested vs 68 pct average.

text.p: Indiana's soybean crop was 27 percent harvested as of Sunday, trailing the five-year average of 68 percent, the Indiana Agricultural Statistics Service said in its weekly report.
Corn was 15 percent harvested, behind 36 percent average.
"Scattered showers slowed corn and soybean harvest early in the week, but harvesting activity was in full swing toward the weekend," the report said.

Average moisture content for corn was 27 percent while soybeans were coming in at an average of 14 percent moisture. Widespread frost in central and northern areas last week further slowed the dry-down pace.

Corn was rated three percent very poor, 10 percent poor, 38 percent fair, 45 percent good and four percent excellent. Soybeans were rated three percent very poor, 13 percent poor, 43 percent fair, 37 percent good and four percent excellent.
Topsoil moisture was rated two percent very short, 13 percent short, 83 percent adequate and two percent surplus.
Pasture and range conditions were rated six percent very poor, 14 percent poor, 49 percent fair, 29 percent good and two percent excellent.
